args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1, with error rate elevated to ~18% (0.18).

Remediation performed:
1. Confirmed current version v2.3.1 unhealthy in all three production regions.
2. Reviewed release history: v2.3.0 was the most recent release healthy in production (v2.2.9 also healthy; v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and itself unhealthy, so it was not a candidate).
3. Initiated rollback to v2.3.0 in all production regions. The first attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state: us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1.
4. Retried the rollback, which completed successfully. All three regions are now on v2.3.0.

Current state: checkout-api is healthy in all regions; error rate has dropped to ~0.2% (0.002).

Follow-up: root cause of the v2.3.1 health-check failures is not yet understood — investigate before any re-deploy of v2.3.1 or v2.3.1-rc. Note the v2.3.1-rc staging build is also unhealthy.

## Summary

**Rollback: complete and verified**
- Found checkout-api on **v2.3.1**, unhealthy in all three production regions with error rate ~18%.
- Release history showed **v2.3.0** as the most recent *production* release with healthy status. (v2.2.9 was also healthy but older; v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and itself unhealthy, so it was not a valid target.)
- First rollback attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error, leaving a **mixed state**: us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on the broken v2.3.1.
- Retried the rollback → completed successfully. All three regions now on **v2.3.0**.
- Verified healthy: `healthy: true`, error rate down from **0.18 → 0.002**.

**Incident: opened**
- **INC-0001** — SEV2, checkout-api, documenting the v2.3.1 failure, the partial-rollout failure and retry, and current healthy state.

**Two things worth flagging for follow-up:**
1. The root cause of the v2.3.1 health-check failures is still unknown — v2.3.1 should not be re-deployed until it's understood.
2. The **v2.3.1-rc staging build is also unhealthy**, which suggests the defect was present before promotion to production. Worth reviewing why it cleared staging gates, since that's the same candidate build lineage.

I did not attempt any new deploy of a never-healthy version, so no change-manager approval was required.
